A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EVER and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Corresponding content can be matched across revisions and relocations; numerical inconsistencies in v6 do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction-quality measurements, rendering demonstrations, timing results and component ablations in Section 6 and the appendix.

after.justification: v6 retains original reconstruction and ablation results and adds benchmark results, quantitative popping measurements and resource comparisons.

M1.justification: v6 corrects the written opacity-based splitting test from a positive exponent in v1 Equation 8 to a negative exponent in Equation 6, making it consistent with the stated near-opaque splitting rule. The renderer, density parameterization, regularizer and initialization remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish an implementation change.

E1.justification: v6 extends systematic reconstruction evaluation beyond Mip-NeRF360 and Zip-NeRF to four scenes from DeepBlending and Tanks&Temples combined. DeepBlending is newly represented, while Tanks&Temples coverage expands beyond the train-scene popping visualization already present in v1 Figure 7.

E2.justification: v6 adds evaluated Mip Splatting rows to the appendix's Zip-NeRF comparison, whereas v1 only cited that method. It also adds SMERF to the qualitative comparison panels. The main table's existing comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: v6 introduces quantitative popping evaluation using StopThePop's FLIP metric at steps 1 and 7 across four scene groups, supplementing v1's visual evaluation. Training GPU-hours and model disk size also become comparison metrics. The retained appendix hyperparameters are unchanged; the changed LPIPS scores do not establish a particular backend or normalization change.

E4.justification: New Table 2 quantitatively tests the central no-popping claim across DeepBlending, Tanks&Temples and indoor/outdoor Mip-NeRF360 scenes. Conversely, v1 Figure 8's visual comparison of rendering ablations is removed. Its associated numerical ablations survive unchanged as v6 Table 3.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. v6's discussion of optical-flow noise explains the popping metric rather than introducing statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes numerous quality and FPS entries: EVER's LPIPS changes from .233 to .194 on Mip-NeRF360 and from .368 to .308 on Zip-NeRF. v6 also adds reconstruction, popping, resource and Mip Splatting results. The appendix retains earlier per-scene scores, so these replacements cannot be treated as established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The splitting inequality gains the missing negative optical-depth sign, correcting an expression that cannot trigger for positive density and scale. The exact rendering integral and inverse-contraction formulas otherwise remain mathematically equivalent; the expanded entry/exit explanation introduces no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: v1's abstract emphasizes exact differentiable volume rendering and the sharpest real-time Zip-NeRF results. v6 foregrounds unrestricted primitive overlap and specifically claims SSIM above offline Zip-NeRF; its conclusion explicitly claims SSIM/LPIPS leadership across both principal benchmarks. The central exactness, consistency and real-time claims remain.

C2.justification: v6 explains why step-7 popping measurements are more reliable relative to optical-flow noise and attributes memory differences to densification rather than per-primitive storage. It removes v1 Table 1's explanation linking Gaussian softness, alignment errors and PSNR. Existing ablation interpretations largely remain.

D1.justification: v6 specifies the spherical-harmonic representation and uniform within-pixel ray jitter, and adds detailed training-cost and storage information. Most appendix implementation details are retained. However, it removes v1's explicit VGG LPIPS backend and [-1,1] normalization disclosure, reducing reproducibility of the revised quality comparison.

R1.justification: Related work adds Condor et al.'s volumetric primitives, Mixture of Volumetric Primitives and VoGE, refining the positioning around overlap handling and approximation. DeepBlending also receives a new citation. Most existing research positioning remains; the duplicate Tanks&Temples reference does not represent another added work.

P1.justification: The abstract, method exposition and conclusion are substantially rewritten around front/back intersections and blending. Density Parameterization becomes Optimization, the splitting criterion moves, and appendix results are reorganized. v6 also introduces an accidental duplication of the opening Results paragraph.

P2.justification: v6 redraws the blending diagram, revises the flatland illustration, restructures Table 1 and adds a popping table. Qualitative examples move between the main text and appendix and gain SMERF columns. The visual ablation figure is removed, and both detailed benchmark tables are consolidated onto the final appendix page.

improvement.justification: Quantitative popping tests, broader benchmark coverage and resource comparisons strengthen v6. However, it introduces unresolved conflicts in central quality results: EVER's Zip-NeRF LPIPS agrees at .368 in v1's main and appendix results, while v6 reports .308 in Table 1 and .368 in Table 4, without retaining the earlier backend/normalization explanation. These reporting problems offset clear evidential gains enough that a reliable net quality judgment is not possible.
